diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: Example dominated by spindly tumour cells showing indistinct cell borders. The nuclei have fine chromatin and small, distinct nucleoli. There are intermingled small lymphocytes.

Example dominated by spindly tumour cells. Positive labelling of the tumour cell nuclei for EBV-encoded small RNAs (EBERs) on in situ hybridization supports the diagnosis of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The tumour cells also show immunoreactivity for cytokeratin and p40 (not shown), supporting their epithelial nature.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: This example is dominated by spindly tumour cells with indistinct cell borders. The nuclei have fine chromatin and prominent nucleoli.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: The nasopharyngeal mucosa shows infiltration by sheets and islands of carcinoma beneath an intact surface epithelium, which shows squamous metaplasia.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: The ulcerated nasopharyngeal mucosa is infiltrated by sheets of carcinoma cells. Necrosis is present.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: An example with amyloid globules among the carcinoma cells.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma
legend: In situ hybridization for EBV-encoded small RNAs (EBERs) shows positive nuclear labelling of all the tumour cells.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, differentiated subtype
legend: The tumour grows in the form of plexiform sheets, showing some resemblance to urothelial carcinoma.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, differentiated subtype
legend: The carcinoma grows in the form of complex anastomosing trabeculae.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, differentiated subtype
legend: The carcinoma cells are polygonal and have a moderate amount of cytoplasm.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, differentiated subtype
legend: Compared with the undifferentiated subtype, the carcinoma cells have more distinct cell borders, a greater amount of cytoplasm, and more chromatin-rich nuclei.
Keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. This tumour is morphologically similar to keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma commonly seen in other head and neck sites.

Keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. This case shows association with EBV. In situ hybridization shows labelling of only a proportion of tumour cells, in contrast to the extensive labelling seen in non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma.

Keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. This carcinoma arose many years after successful radiation therapy for nasopharyngeal non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma (EBV). The carcinoma is very well differentiated, with minimal nuclear atypia or pleomorphism. A diagnosis of malignancy is supported by the presence of stromal invasion. In situ hybridization for EBV-encoded small RNAs (EBERs) is negative (not shown).

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: The large syncytial-appearing tumour cells have vesicular nuclei and large nucleoli. The nuclei commonly appear crowded and overlapping.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: Irregular islands of large tumour cells with indistinct cell borders, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli. Identification of the cohesive growth in the lymphoid background gives a clue to the epithelial nature of the tumour.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: In some cases, nuclear pleomorphism is more marked; there is marked variation in nuclear size, and the nuclei show irregular folding.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: A typical example with an island of large syncytial-appearing tumour cells with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli. The background is rich in lymphocytes.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: There are sheets of large tumour cells with indistinct cell borders, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli. The epithelial nature of the tumour may not be evident without the identification of areas forming a discrete interface with the lymphoid stroma.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: In undifferentiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma, there can be foci showing subtle squamous differentiation: the tumour cells have more distinct cell borders and a great amount of eosinophilic cytoplasm (lower right).

Basaloid squamous cell carcinoma. The tumour comprises nests and festoons of basaloid cells interspersed with variable amounts of hyaline to mucoid stroma. There are foci of abrupt squamous differentiation.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: This example shows a lymphoepithelial carcinoma morphology. Aggregates of syncytial-appearing carcinoma cells with large vesicular nuclei and distinct nucleoli are intimately admixed with many lymphocytes and plasma cells.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: In this example, the nasopharyngeal carcinoma infiltrate in the mucosa is more subtle. Anastomosing irregular small nests of carcinoma occur beneath an intact surface epithelium.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, undifferentiated subtype
legend: This example is dominated by spindly tumour cells, mimicking sarcoma. The spindly cells form interlacing fascicles. Focally, there is a reticulated pattern (lower-right corner).

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma
legend: Immunostaining for pancytokeratin (MNF116) highlights the irregular aggregates of carcinoma cells in a lymphoid cell–rich background.

diagnosis: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma
legend: Immunostaining for p40 highlights the irregular clusters of carcinoma cells in the nasopharyngeal mucosa. The p40 positivity supports the squamous nature of the carcinoma cells.

PET of a patient newly diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma. This demonstrates avid FDG uptake by the primary tumour in the nasopharynx, bilateral metastatic cervical lymph nodes, and distant metastases to a right axillary lymph node and L1 vertebral body. Normal uptake is noted in the brain, bladder, and kidneys.

Exposure to environmental carcinogens induces various genetic lesions (e.g. deletions in chromosomes 3p and 9p) and subsequent inactivation of key tumour suppressor genes (such as CDKN2A and TGFBR2) that predispose to EBV infection and transformation of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. In nasopharyngeal epithelial cells persistently infected with EBV, the presence of episomal viral genomes and expression of latency II viral proteins (EBNA1, LMP1, and LMP2) and non-coding RNAs (EBV-encoded small RNAs [EBERs], microRNA-BARTs, and BART long non-coding RNAs) promote genome instability, induce global DNA methylation, and activate virtually all cancer hallmarks. Clonal expansion of EBV-transformed nasopharyngeal epithelial cells leads to the accumulation of multiple genetic and epigenetic events driving NPC progression. The convergence of somatic genomic alterations (e.g. mutations in the proinflammatory NF-κB pathway and in components of antigen presentation machinery) and EBV latent gene expression (e.g. of LMP1 and BNLF2a) modulates the tumour microenvironment and immune escape. Other acquired genetic changes (including alterations of TP53, genes involved in chromatin remodelling, and components of the PI3K/MAPK pathway) contribute to tumour progression, occurrence of local recurrences, and distant metastasis {34194007}. HLA, human leukocyte antigen; LOH, loss of heterozygosity; MHC, major histocompatibility complex; NPI, nasopharyngeal inlet; SNP, small nucleotide polymorphism.

Areas of well-developed keratinization are noted in this nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
